title: Rule Orchestrator and Runtime Access Harness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build a scalable policy evaluation orchestration service (Rule Orchestrator) and a lightweight runtime access harness that can be injected into API, runtime, and console request paths. The orchestrator compiles declarative rules into optimized evaluation plans, supports conditional/contextual clauses (time windows, KV claims, session attributes), and emits enriched audit events suitable for downstream pipelines. The runtime harness is an interceptor library for API gateway, inference runtime, and console frontends that performs fast allow/deny checks, attaches decision metadata to trace/span, and can defer to orchestrator for complex decisions. The deliverable must cover: evaluation semantics, fallback mode for soft-deny, explainability payloads in audit logs, SSO/SAML claim mapping hooks, and an admin consent flow for high-privilege grants.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator accepts a policy DSL and produces an execution plan within acceptable compile latency (<150ms median for 200 rules)
Runtime harness returns decision within SLO: 95th percentile <12ms for cached simple-policies; defers to orchestrator for complex policies with clear timeout fallback
Audit events include decision id, policy version, rule trace (up to 4 hops), principal claims snapshot, and request fingerprint
Admin console can show explainability for a decision and trigger admin-consent workflow that attaches approval token to session
Integration tests for API+runtime+console paths with SSO/SAML claim mappings and consent flow pass in CI
design_notes: Policy DSL: JSON/YAML with 'principals', 'actions', 'resources', 'conditions' and optional 'temporal' blocks. Conditions support prefix caching hints to accelerate runtime path.
Planner: compile-time facts extraction -> predicate indexing -> ordered short-circuit evaluation. Plans are serializable and pinned to policy-version for deterministic audits.

Runtime harness: minimal dependency, provides in-memory LRU for recent plan fragments, exposes a gRPC/HTTP client to orchestrator for heavy evals. On orchestrator timeout, harness applies configured fallback (deny-by-default or permissive with audit flag).

Explainability: store compact rule trace tokens in audit sink; reconstruct full trace on-demand in Console using policy-version and trace token. Avoid including PII directly in audit event; reference claim snapshots stored in encrypted audit blob.
SSO/SAML: provide pluggable claim mappers that normalize incoming assertions into canonical principals used by policy evaluation. Mapper chain will be configurable per-tenant.
Admin consent: lightweight approval token flow with TTL, sign+nonce to prevent replay. Consent events are auditable and revocable via Admin Console.
Backward compatibility: support a compatibility layer that translates RBAC v1 allow/deny sets into v2 DSL for migration period.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal canary): deploy harness to staging runtime and internal console flag. Route 5% of internal traffic through orchestrator for complex policies.
Phase 2 (beta customers): enable on selected customer orgs with monitoring and opt-out. Collect audit enrichment correctness metrics.
Phase 3 (gradual): move default policy checks in API gateway to harness with orchestrator fallback; increase traffic incrementally while verifying SLOs.
Rollback: feature flag to switch harness to pass-through and set orchestrator_mode=off. Emergency revoke uses admin token expirer.
test_plan: Unit tests: policy compiler, predicate index, plan serializer/verifier
Integration tests: harness + orchestrator + audit sink with simulated SAML assertions
Performance tests: synthetic traffic with policy distributions to validate compile latency and eval SLOs
Security tests: fuzzing policy inputs, replay attack simulation for consent tokens, audit log tamper detection
Chaos tests: orchestrator failures, network partitions, and harness fallback behavior validation
